correctness.rationale: The PCF condition on a cubic ladder is equivalent to the two explicit forbidden equalities in every three-column window, along with proper edges. A local three-color transition is either a cyclic forward/reverse move or an impossible swap; direction changes fail the same neighborhood constraint. Therefore a three-color pattern cannot satisfy the Möbius row-swap seam. The explicit four-palette words (ABC)^q, (ABC)^qD, (ABC)^qAC satisfy the forbidden equalities at all widths. The 84-state transfer and its row-exchange involution exactly encode all named PCF colorings, including twisted closure. Both full 42-by-42 characteristic polynomials are computed by exact integer Faddeev-LeVerrier in the attached standalone checker. Their determinant traces prove the rational generating series and the Lucas twist correction for all widths; direct small-graph tests are corroboration only.

value.rationale: Möbius ladders are a natural canonical infinite cubic family, and PCF coloring imposes genuinely local unique-neighbor constraints with a global row-swap obstruction. The result determines not just an upper bound but an exact four-color minimum at every width, an all-length named optimal-coloring generating function, and a nontrivial explicit spectral twist correction relative to circular ladders. The exact correction detects exceptional equality at width five and is derived from an involutive transfer decomposition useful in other strip-graph enumerations. These are structural classification and enumeration results, not a routine relabeling of the existing general subcubic upper bound.
residual_risks: Not claimed for other cubic families or color-palette sizes; historical-priority uncertainty remains.
